Publications and displays, centralized payment of bills, publication of publicity literature in different languages about the achievements and development programs of the government, cultural programmes, publicity of achievements of the Government of Bihar within the state and through information and public relations created by the department. . Vision To disseminate and propagate government policies, programmes, schemes and achievements, effectively for public awareness. Documentation of progress and achievements of various department. To know and understand the mood, perception and feedback of people on different issues by analysis of news published in the media and to arrange quick response of governments views/ point among general public through media as necessary. To disseminate policies, programmes and achievements of various departments for educating people and mass communication by performing role of facilitator by using various, method and resources of educating people and mass communication. Formation of creativeness for publicity of programmes, schemes and achievements of various departments through poster, pamphlet, folder, booklet, etc. and to facilitate the advertisement work. national_raw_news.title: 46 mins ago | National 471 Har Ghar Tiranga campaign begins with multiple events across country
national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 9, 2026 8:53 PM Har Ghar Tiranga campaign begins with multiple events across country The Har Ghar Tiranga campaign is being celebrated nationwide to foster a sense of patriotism among citizens, strengthen national unity, and promote India’s cultural heritage. The campaign marks the fifth year of the Har Ghar Tiranga initiative, which began in 2022 and has since evolved into one of the country’s largest public participation movements. The initiative is aimed at encouraging citizens to hoist the National Flag and participate in activities celebrating patriotism, national unity and India’s cultural heritage. This year’s campaign holds special significance as it coincides with the 150th anniversary of India’s National Song, “Vande Mataram,” bringing together the National Flag and the National Song in a unique celebration of patriotism. As part of the celebrations, mass singing of Vande Mataram will be organised across the country. In Delhi, as part of the campaign, Lok Sabha BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj paid floral tribute at the memorial of Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya in Malviya Nagar followed by a Tiranga Yatra from Pilanji Village to Greater Kailash. Speaking to the media, Ms Swaraj said that this Independence Day is particularly special as India marks its 80th. She added that the BJP has launched a week-long campaign starting today, during which party office-bearers and workers will visit the memorials of national heroes and martyrs. national_raw_news.title: 48 mins ago | Regional News 67 Jharkhand govt agrees to scrap JPSC Prelims exams over allegations of irregularities, rejects CGL...
national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 9, 2026 8:57 PM Jharkhand govt agrees to scrap JPSC Prelims exams over allegations of irregularities, rejects CGL cancellation demand The Jharkhand government has reached an agreement on most of the demands of students protesting against alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC examinations. State Minister Sudivya Kumar Sonu said, the government has agreed to cancel the 14th JPSC Preliminary Examination and the 2023-25 backlog examinations. The Minister stated this while talking to media following talks between the state government and protesting students today. He said, the govenment has also agreed to an Enforcement Directorate probe into alleged financial irregularities, a CID investigation into criminal aspects and the setting up of a fast-track court to ensure chargesheets are filed within 90 days. An expert committee comprising representatives from The Indian Institute of Technology (Indian School of Mines) Dhanbad, Indian Institute of Management-Ranchi and XLRI will also be constituted to recommend reforms in the examination system. However, no agreement was reached on the students’ demands for cancellation of the JSSC CGL examination and a CBI probe. The students said their agitation would continue. Meanwhile, the three sitting members of Jharkhand Public Service Commission, Dr Ajita Bhattacharya, Dr Jameel Ahmed, and Dr Anima Hansda have resigned from their posts after being summoned by the CID for questioning tomorrow. Jharkhand Governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar has accepted their resignations. national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 9, 2026 8:57 PM Operation Sindoor Sent Global Message of India’s Zero-Tolerance Approach to Terrorism: Rajnath Singh Lucknow: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh addresses during the inauguration of the Nausena Shaurya Vatika in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, on Saturday, May 30, 2026. (Photo: IANS/PIB) Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today said that Operation Sindoor sent a global message that India will go to any extent to ensure the safety of its citizens while protecting the sindoor worn by the women of this country. The minister said this at the inaugural event of the Sindoor Maharaktadan Yatra Blood Donation Camp at Base Hospital in New Delhi. The Defence Minister commended the Indian Defence Forces for eliminating terrorists and their handlers based in Pakistan and ensuring that those who dared to cast an evil eye on India faced dire consequences. Underlining Sindoor Maharaktadan Yatra, Mr Singh asserted that while Operation Sindoor showcased courage, the mega blood donation camp represents compassion. He said that around one thousand wrestlers and athletes from Maharashtra were among the donors who participated in the camp. He added that it demonstrated the spirit of selfless service and solidarity with the Defence Forces. Defence Minister said that every blood donor and recipient is, in their own way, serving the nation. He urged the people, particularly the youth, to make blood donation a culture. national_raw_news.title: 53 mins ago | National 51 Over 1.25 Crore Houses Sanctioned Under PMAY-Urban So Far: Govt
national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 9, 2026 8:58 PM Over 1.25 Crore Houses Sanctioned Under PMAY-Urban So Far: Govt The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has said that over one crore 25 lakh houses have been sanctioned so far under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban (PMAY-U) and PMAY-U 2.0. Of these, more than one crore houses have been completed and handed over to beneficiaries across the country with around one crore of the houses allotted to women. The Ministry said over two lakh nine thousand houses were sanctioned under PMAY-U 2.0 for economically weaker section families in 16 states and Union Territories including Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Jammu and Kashmir, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Manipur, Odisha, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand. Of these, over two lakh three thousand houses have been allotted to women. More than 16,600 houses have been sanctioned for senior citizens, while around 22 thousand are for Scheduled Caste beneficiaries, over 14 thousand for Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries and more than 75 thousand for Other Backward Classes. During the meeting of the Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee, Housing and Urban Affairs Secretary Satendra Singh reviewed the progress of the scheme and stressed timely implementation, release of funds, effective monitoring and close coordination among all stakeholders to ensure that benefits reach every eligible urban family. national_raw_news.title: Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu Rejects Trump’s 15-Point Gaza Plan
national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 9, 2026 7:50 PM Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu Rejects Trump’s 15-Point Gaza Plan Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected US President Donald Trump’s 15-point plan for Gaza. Speaking at a cabinet meeting today, Prime Minister Netanyahu insisted that Israel will not withdraw its forces until Palestinian armed group Hamas is genuinely disarmed and it would continue to act against threats to Israeli forces and civilians. He said Israeli officials are now in discussion with US officials about how to move forward. President Trump’s Board of Peace last month said that it had reached an agreement aimed at the complete disarmament of Hamas in Gaza. However, Hamas has said that surrendering its heavy weapons would depend on Israel ending all forms of aggression and withdrawing its forces from the territory. Despite an initial ceasefire agreement reached last October, Israel has continued to carry out strikes in Gaza. national_raw_news.title: No Direct Talks with US, Exchange of messages through intermediaries: Iran
national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 9, 2026 6:05 PM No Direct Talks with US, Exchange of messages through intermediaries: Iran Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi today said, his country is not currently engaged in direct negotiations with the United States, while messages between the two sides are being exchanged through intermediaries. According to his statement carried by Iranian state media, Mr Araghchi said, several countries were continuing efforts to create conditions for the resumption of negotiations between Tehran and Washington. He said, Tehran would not return to direct talks with the US until Washington ends its violations of the 14-point memorandum of understanding signed between the two sides in June. Yesterday, Mr Araghchi said, the deal with Oman on a legal mechanism for managing traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is very close, but reopening the strategic waterway will be subject to additional conditions, including compensation from the US over the latter’s violations of the memorandum. The statement comes as a US official on Friday stated that progress has been made in talks between Iran and Oman, which could lead to the reopening of the strategic Strait of Hormuz and restore oil exports disrupted by the five-month-old conflict. national_raw_news.title: Over 3.8 Lakh People Affected by monsoon, cyclones in Philippines
national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 9, 2026 4:47 PM Over 3.8 Lakh People Affected by monsoon, cyclones in Philippines The enhanced southwest monsoon and tropical cyclones have affected more than 3.8 lakh people across eight regions in the Philippines. According to the Philippine News Agency, 1.1 lakh families were affected, with six deaths and seven injuries reported. The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council of the Philippines said 86 evacuation centres have been activated, sheltering about 7,300 people. Another 3,700 people are staying outside evacuation centres. The National Weather Service agency PAGASA warned that the southwest monsoon will continue to bring heavy rain to Metro Manila and several provinces in Luzon. It warned of possible flash floods and landslides in Ilocos Sur, La Union, Abra, Benguet, Zambales, Bataan and Occidental Mindoro. Scattered rain and thunderstorms are also expected in the Visayas and parts of Mindanao. PAGASA said Typhoon Dolphin is strengthening the southwest monsoon, with rough to very rough seas expected off extreme Northern Luzon. national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 9, 2026 12:56 PM India’s medal tally rises to 3 at World Athletics Under-20 Championships India’s medal tally rises to three at the World Athletics Under-20 Championships in the United States. India’s Basant Kumar Meghwal wins a silver in the high jump, while Shahnavaz Khan wins a bronze in the long jump today. In the men’s high jump, 19-year-old Meghwal cleared his personal best of 2.21 metres to win a silver medal. He became the first Indian to win a medal in the high jump at the World U-20 Championships. Algeria’s Younes Ayachi won the gold, while Great Britain’s Otis Poole took the bronze. In the men’s long jump, Shahnavaz clinched bronze with a best effort of 7.84 metres. The 18-year-old produced his best jump in his third attempt. Italy’s Daniele Inzoli won the gold medal with a jump of 7.97 metres, while Australia’s Mason McGroder took silver with a personal best of 7.96 metres. Earlier, in the javelin throw, Ashish Yadav won silver and became the second Indian after Neeraj Chopra to win at the World Athletics U20 Championships. Yadav produced his best throw of 74.09 metres in the third round yesterday. national_raw_news.title: Sagnik-Sayantan win Gold medal in Under-31 Pairs at 9th World Bridge Federation Youth Transnational Championships 14 hours ago 266
national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 9, 2026 8:35 AM Sagnik-Sayantan win Gold medal in Under-31 Pairs at 9th World Bridge Federation Youth Transnational Championships Sagnik Roy and Sayantan Kushari won the gold medal in the Under-31 Pairs at the 9th World Youth Transnational Championships in Hefei, China, yesterday. In the first elimination round, 34 pairs competed and the top 14 advanced to Flight A, including the Indian duo. They then competed in a round-robin format, with Sagnik and Sayantan finishing on top with 377.67 match points. M Fereneca and F Katusich of Croatia finished second with 357.78 match points, while China’s J Han and Z Wang took the third spot with 335.92 match points. national_raw_news.title: Asian Junior Weightlifting C’ships: India Secures Gold, Silver in Men’s 60kg Category 08 Aug 2026 | 9:40 PM 229
national_raw_news.content: News On AIR | August 8, 2026 9:40 PM Asian Junior Weightlifting C’ships: India Secures Gold, Silver in Men’s 60kg Category Indian lifters continued their impressive performance at the Asian Junior Weightlifting Championships in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, today, with a gold and a silver medal in the men’s junior 60-kilogram category. Tomchou Meetei won a total of three medals – gold in the overall category, bronze in the snatch and silver in the clean and jerk. He finished with a combined lift of 266 kilograms. Gurunaidu Sanapathi bagged two medals – silver in the overall category and silver in the snatch, along with bronze in the clean and jerk. He finished with a total lift of 265 kilograms. The two Indian lifters finished just one kilogram apart in the overall standings, giving India a one-two finish in the category.
